claims: C1 an instruction is superseded when a later message at the same authority level contains an instruction that contradicts it
C2 an instruction is superseded when a later message at the same authority level contains an instruction that overrides it
C3 an instruction is superseded when a later message at the same authority level contains an instruction that otherwise makes it irrelevant, e.g. by changing the context of the request

concepts.name: superseded_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that is made irrelevant by a later instruction at the same authority level
concepts.inference: the PROVIDES contract assigns this predicate and its meaning; the source text defines 'superseded' as the condition this module encodes

concepts.name: applicable_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction that applies to the current request, determined by filtering candidate instructions
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this predicate and its meaning; this node's text presupposes that instructions are filtered for applicability without defining the filter

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level H outranks level L in the authority hierarchy root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this predicate and its meaning; this node's text presupposes the ranking without stating it

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is the root authority level, the highest in the authority hierarchy, assigned to Model Spec 'root' sections
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this predicate and its meaning; this node's text presupposes the authority levels without defining them

concepts.name: instruction_in_message
concepts.gloss: instruction I appears in message M
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of an instruction 'in a later message', so a relation between an instruction and its message must exist

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of instructions 'at the same level', so each instruction must carry an authority level

concepts.name: later_message
concepts.gloss: message M1 is later than message M2 in the conversation
concepts.inference: the source text speaks of a 'later message', so an ordering relation between messages must exist

concepts.name: makes_irrelevant
concepts.gloss: instruction I1 otherwise makes instruction I2 irrelevant, e.g. by changing the context of the request

ontology.gloss: I1 is superseded because a later instruction at the same level contradicts it
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I1), instruction_in_message(I1, M1), instruction_in_message(I2, M2), later_message(M2, M1), instruction_level(I1, L), instruction_level(I2, L), contradicts(I2, I1)

ontology.gloss: I1 is superseded because a later instruction at the same level overrides it
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I1), instruction_in_message(I1, M1), instruction_in_message(I2, M2), later_message(M2, M1), instruction_level(I1, L), instruction_level(I2, L), overrides(I2, I1)

ontology.gloss: I1 is superseded because a later instruction at the same level otherwise makes it irrelevant
ontology.body: applicable_instruction(I1), instruction_in_message(I1, M1), instruction_in_message(I2, M2), later_message(M2, M1), instruction_level(I1, L), instruction_level(I2, L), makes_irrelevant(I2, I1)
